Clean pass with caveats. (1) The IRW item codes carry no item content: data/KoreanNursing_Park_2017.R runs read.table(header=TRUE) over the Dataverse file 'Jeehp-14-20_raw data.tab', which has NO header row, so the first examinee's 50 zeros and ones became the column names and make.names/make.unique turned them into X0, X1, X1.1, X0.1 ... X0.39. Re-running that line reproduces all 50 live codes in order, so position i = question i; that examinee is absent from the live table, which holds 740 of the study's 741 respondents. (2) resp runs the unusual way round: 1 = INCORRECT, 0 = correct. For all 50 items, (741 - Supplement 7's published number of correct answers) minus that examinee's own score equals the live count of resp==1 EXACTLY (e.g. q1 741-332-0 = 409 = live X0; q13 741-26-1 = 714 = live X1.3). (3) The exam was administered in Korean; neither the article, its seven supplements nor the Dataverse deposit contains a single Hangul character (checked explicitly across suppl1-4, 6, 7), so the fallback applies: the authors' own English from Supplement 7 sits in the base fields, the _translated columns are empty, language=Korean. (4) The five answer options are printed inside item_text after the stem, as Supplement 7 prints them, because resp is a 0/1 score and cannot carry a chosen option; option_text holds the accuracy labels Correct/Incorrect for resp 0/1, which are IRW's words for a direction established from the data, not published labels. (5) No answer key is published; correct_response was derived from Supplement 7's own upper/lower-27% response-distribution tables (the keyed option is the one whose High-27% and Low-27% counts equal the item's High/Low correct counts), unique for 49 of 50 items; item 5's table omits the correct/wrong counts, and its option 3 takes 336/400 = 84% of the extreme groups, matching its published 84% correct-answer rate. (6) Two figures are not reproducible in text: the electronic fetal monitoring graph in case 15 (referenced by q33) and the family health assessment tool / ecomap in case 19 (referenced by q44); q47 refers to 'the underlined information' in case 20's vignette and the underlining is lost in a plain-text transcript. (7) Supplement 7's own numbers are internally inconsistent for q31: it prints 181 correct out of 741 (24.4%) but a correct-answer rate of 27%; the live data agrees with 181. (8) irw-validate WARN name_charset ('KoreanNursing_Park_2017' is not lowercase): a property of the LIVE IRW table name, not of this itemtext file -- the itemtext table must be named <table>__items to join, so the case cannot be changed here. Not an itemtext defect; it is an upstream table-naming issue. (9) ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK (Step 5b, 2026-09-08): the two claims headed for public notes were confirmed independently of the agent's report. irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE) returns n_rows=37000 = 740 x 50 with n=740 on every one of the 50 items, confirming that exactly one of the study's 741 respondents was consumed as the header row; and the live item codes are literally X0, X0.1, X0.10, ... , i.e. make.names/make.unique artifacts, confirming the codes carry no item content. The reversed 1=INCORRECT coding was re-derived by verify_batch.R re-running verify_KoreanNursing_Park_2017.R end to end (VERDICT: PASS), and the shipped CSV encodes it consistently: option_text is 'Correct' at resp=0 and 'Incorrect' at resp=1 for all 50 items, with no exceptions. (10) DISCLOSURE OWED: check_provenance.R reports this table as shipping an answer key this project derived rather than transcribed (key_source=derived_from_responses) with no entry yet on the public issues page. Under the 2026-09-03 ruling it owes a line on itemtext_issues.qmd. The site checkout is currently on branch itemtext/disclosure-backlog-2026-09-08 so the check was reported but not enforced; the entry still has to be written before upload.

STEP 3b CLEAN: the table really is the CARE Measure and not one of the three sibling instruments in the same deposit -- the S3 File workbook (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0177758.s003, one sheet Nonverbal_empathy_study_1c, 1377 rows) holds COMP1-5 (competence), WARM1-4 (warmth), CARE1-10 and PANASPOS/NEG1-10 side by side, and data/kraft_todd_2017_empathic_nonverbal.py melts exactly [f"CARE{i}" for i in range(1,11)] into this table; the live item set from irw::irw_fetch is CARE1..CARE10 and the live resp set is 1-6, which is the CARE Measure's six-column form (Poor/Fair/Good/Very good/Excellent/Does not apply) and not the warmth-competence 0-4 scale or the PANAS 1-5 scale. QUOTED RESTRICTION from the rights holder: "The CARE Measure is free to use for non-commercial purposes and is widely used in the UK for appraisal and revalidation. ... If you are wishing to use the CARE Measure outside of the UK, for research or education, or any other purpose, then you need to seek permission from Professor Stewart Mercer, who developed and validated the measure, and holds the copyright. The measure cannot be used outside the UK without his permission prior to starting your research. There can be no changes made to the wording, without permission, and all translated versions into different languages must remain under his copyright." (https://caremeasure.stir.ac.uk/, fetched 2026-09-08, cached at itemtext/.cache/kraft_todd_2017_care_measure/). That is a stated non-commercial restriction plus a permission gate on the instrument itself, the free-but-restricted shape ruled on for TIMSS, PROMIS and HEXACO; under irw#1945 (2026-09-05) and irw#1955 (2026-09-06) the rights holder's stated use restriction overrides the licence of the deposit the wording would have been taken from, which here is PLOS CC BY 4.0 and governs the response data only. MAPPING BANKED so a reversal is a re-run, not a restart: the study's own S2 File (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0177758.s002, .docx, cached) reproduces all 10 CARE stems in order with their parenthetical elaborations and the six response columns "Poor / Fair / Good / Very good / Excellent / Does not apply", so a re-run would ship mapping_basis=paper_order (the S2 layout numbers nothing, but its order is the canonical Mercer 2004 order and matches CARE1..CARE10), text_source=study_materials, English administration (no _translated columns), option_text Poor=1 Fair=2 Good=3 Very good=4 Excellent=5 "Does not apply"=6, and instructions blank (the S2 layout prints no instruction line above the CARE block; the article renders items as "How was the doctor at showing care and compassion (...)?"). Direction confirmed from the data rather than assumed: mean CARE by empathy condition is 1.65-2.52 (condemp=0) vs 3.04-3.98 (condemp=1) on all ten items, so higher = better and 1=Poor..5=Excellent, with 6 an out-of-order "Does not apply" category rather than a scale point. Per-item n is 1372 for all ten items in the source workbook and matches the live table. Corroboration available if it is ever unblocked: CARE7 "Being positive" is the highest-rated item (3.26 vs 2.39-2.72 for the rest) and the two items least applicable to a silent video vignette carry the most 6s (CARE2 "Letting you tell your story" 88, CARE9 "Helping you to take control" 70, against 2-48 elsewhere). NOT an access failure: the article, the S2 .docx, the S3 .xlsx and the rights page all fetched cleanly. RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry right now would reach the same verdict. Only a change in the IRW ruling on free-but-permission-gated instruments, or written permission from Professor Mercer, would flip it.

Clean pass with two caveats. (1) Within-block order is PARTIAL: the S2 File lists the 5 competence traits in order but attaches no COMP* codes, and while COMP4=Competitive and COMP3=Independent are pinned by the data (lowest mean / most 'Does not apply' / weakest inter-item r, in that rank order), Competent / Confident / Intelligent on COMP1 / COMP2 / COMP5 rest on presentation order alone - the paper publishes no per-item statistics.
